correctness.rationale: Under t=((-ln y)/lambda)^k, the transformed integrand is t^a exp((p-1)lambda*t^(1/k)-p*t/2)(1-exp(-t))^(-p/2), a=(p-1)(k-1)/k. At zero it behaves like t^(a-p/2), requiring k>2-2/p. At infinity for p<1 all exponential terms decay, for p>1 the sign is governed by whether t^(1/k) is sublinear (k>1), superlinear (k<1), or linear (k=1, requiring lambda<p/[2(p-1)]). Combining with p<2 when k=1 gives exactly three branches; equality at either endpoint fails. Direct boundary p=2,k=1 gives square-density ~(pi^2 lambda)^(-1)(1-y)^(-1). All p ranges are analytically exhausted without a finite-to-infinite extrapolation.
